Thanks for the recap and for sending the attachments. A few clarifying items from our side so legal can triage quickly:

Hi Samir -

Appreciate the clear list - answering inline below and attaching our DPA annex for the items that map to contract language.

1) Controller/Processor: Redwood acts as a processor for customer-provided input and resulting model outputs. We do not assert joint-controller status in our standard DPA; any deviation would be explicitly negotiated. (See section 2 of the attached annex.)

2) Subprocessors: Our current subprocessors are listed in Appendix A of the DPA annex (examples: AWS for compute/storage, FastLogs Inc. for logging pipeline, PagerDuty for incident management). We provide 30-day notice for non-critical additions and immediate notice for security-critical changes.

3) Breach notice: Redwood's commitment is to notify customers within 72 hours of confirming a security incident affecting customer data and provide a root-cause and remediation plan within 30 days. This is in line with your requirement - we'll add the specific timing language to the DPA if needed.

4) Logs & retention: We can configure log retention per-account. By default request logs are retained for 90 days; we offer an option to disable long-term retention of request payloads or reduce to a custom retention (e.g., 30 days). We recommend disabling payload retention for PII-sensitive workloads and using token-level billing traces only.

Attached: Redwood_DPA_Annex.pdf (contains Appendix A subprocessors and breach/notice language). I've also attached a filled version of your Aurora_DPA_Questions.docx with short answers.

Proposed next step: Legal-to-legal call to confirm any contract edits. Ben - can you and Monica join a 30-minute call Tue 11/30 at 10:00 AM PST if that works for Aurora legal? If not, propose two alternate times and I'll coordinate.

Samir/Priya - if you want the written edits to DPA language before the call we can send a marked-up version 1 business day prior.

Best,
Marissa
